nodes.label: Sun
nodes.definition: Sites that receive six or more hours of direct sun in summer.

nodes.label: Shade
nodes.definition: Sites with little or no direct sun: filtered light under a canopy or deep shade on the north side of buildings and under dense trees.

nodes.label: Part shade
nodes.definition: Sites with roughly three to six hours of direct sun, or sun for only part of the day.

nodes.label: Full sun
nodes.definition: Six or more hours of direct sun in summer; no overhead canopy.

nodes.label: Full sun only if soil kept moist
nodes.definition: Takes full sun only where the soil does not dry out; in dry sun it scorches or stalls.

nodes.label: Part sun/part shade
nodes.definition: Three to six hours of direct sun, or dappled light for much of the day.

nodes.label: Filtered shade
nodes.definition: Light reaching the plant through a tree canopy or lattice all day; bright but never direct for long.

nodes.label: Deep shade
nodes.definition: Less than about two hours of direct sun; under dense canopy or on the north side of buildings.

nodes.label: Sheltered
nodes.definition: A position protected from strong or cold wind, for example near a wall or inside a planting.

nodes.label: Acidic
nodes.definition: Soil with pH below about 6.5, typical of coastal BC under conifers.

nodes.label: Alkaline
nodes.definition: Soil with pH above about 7.5, usually over limestone or where lime has been added.

nodes.label: Bog
nodes.definition: Permanently wet, peaty, acidic ground with standing water close to the surface.

nodes.label: Humus rich
nodes.definition: Dark soil high in decomposed organic matter; holds moisture and nutrients well.

nodes.label: Rocky or gravelly or dry
nodes.definition: Thin, stony or sandy ground that drains fast and holds little water or nutrient.

nodes.label: Well-drained
nodes.definition: Soil through which water passes freely, so roots are never left standing in water.

nodes.label: dry
nodes.definition: Little available soil moisture for long periods; relies on rain or drought tolerance.

nodes.label: average
nodes.definition: Ordinary garden moisture: rain plus occasional watering, neither dry nor wet for long.

nodes.label: moist
nodes.definition: Soil that stays damp but not waterlogged, such as a shaded bed or a slope base.

nodes.label: wet
nodes.definition: Soil often saturated: pond margins, ditches, poorly drained low ground.

nodes.label: wide range
nodes.definition: Tolerates anything from dry to wet once established.

nodes.label: Exposed

nodes.label: Tree

nodes.label: Upright

nodes.definition: Landscape use 'Winter interest': At its best in winter.

nodes.label: Woodland margin
nodes.definition: Landscape use 'Woodland margin': Grows at the edge of trees, in part shade.

nodes.label: pollinator
nodes.definition: Flowers feed bees and other pollinating insects.

nodes.label: bird food
nodes.definition: Fruit or seed eaten by birds.

nodes.label: wildlife cover
nodes.definition: Dense growth that shelters birds or small animals.

nodes.label: nitrogen fixer
nodes.definition: Roots host bacteria that add nitrogen to the soil.

nodes.label: erosion control
nodes.definition: Roots hold soil on slopes and banks.

nodes.label: habitat structure
nodes.definition: Adds a layer or structure other species live in.

nodes.label: Spring
nodes.definition: March to May in Vancouver: leaf-out and most flowering.

nodes.label: Summer
nodes.definition: June to August: growth, fruit set and the dry season.

nodes.label: Autumn
nodes.definition: September to November: fruit, fall colour, the rains return.

nodes.label: Winter
nodes.definition: December to February: dormancy, evergreen structure, wet and mild.

nodes.label: January
nodes.definition: January, month 1; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: February
nodes.definition: February, month 2; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: March
nodes.definition: March, month 3; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: April
nodes.definition: April, month 4; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: May
nodes.definition: May, month 5; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: June
nodes.definition: June, month 6; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: July
nodes.definition: July, month 7; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: August
nodes.definition: August, month 8; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: September
nodes.definition: September, month 9; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: October
nodes.definition: October, month 10; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: November
nodes.definition: November, month 11; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: December
nodes.definition: December, month 12; used for flowering, fruiting and observation dates.

nodes.label: Young plant
nodes.definition: In its first years after planting, before it reaches its character size (sources say 'in youth').

nodes.label: Establishing
nodes.definition: Roughly five to ten years in: filling out, not yet full size.

nodes.label: Established
nodes.definition: Settled in and growing at full vigour; in the City of Vancouver inventory approximated by trunk diameter ≥ 20 cm (methods M2).

nodes.label: Mature / 20+ years
nodes.definition: At or near its full size; USDA figures given 'at 20 years' map here.

nodes.label: Global
nodes.definition: Sources or figures not tied to a region (for example RHS species profiles read as general).

nodes.label: United Kingdom
nodes.definition: UK growing conditions, the basis of RHS plant profiles: milder, wetter summers than Vancouver.

nodes.label: North America
nodes.definition: Continental sources such as USDA PLANTS, read as US-wide.

nodes.label: St. Louis, Missouri
nodes.definition: Missouri Botanical Garden's growing conditions: hot humid summers, cold winters.

nodes.label: Pacific Northwest
nodes.definition: Coastal Pacific Northwest from Oregon to BC: mild wet winters, dry summers.

nodes.label: Willamette Valley, Oregon
nodes.definition: Oregon State University's reference region: similar climate to Vancouver, hotter summers.

nodes.label: British Columbia
nodes.definition: Province-level evidence such as E-Flora BC and ISCBC.

nodes.label: Metro Vancouver
nodes.definition: The region the database serves: City of Vancouver and its municipalities, Canadian hardiness 8a–8b.

nodes.label: City of Vancouver
nodes.definition: The city itself, the area the public tree inventory covers.

nodes.label: North Vancouver
nodes.definition: North Shore municipality: wetter and shadier than the city, used by practitioner observations.

nodes.label: Native
nodes.definition: Occurs naturally in the region without having been introduced by people.

nodes.label: Native to BC west of the Cascades
nodes.definition: Grows naturally in coastal BC, the Vancouver region included.

nodes.label: Native to North America
nodes.definition: Native to the continent but not to coastal BC.

nodes.label: Non-native
nodes.definition: Introduced from elsewhere; not naturally occurring here.

nodes.label: Invasive in BC
nodes.definition: Introduced and spreading in BC to the harm of native habitat.

nodes.label: Not listed as invasive
nodes.definition: Does not appear on BC or ISCBC invasive lists.

nodes.label: On a watch list
nodes.definition: Flagged for monitoring; not regulated.

nodes.label: Regulated in BC
nodes.definition: Control required under BC regulation.

nodes.label: Prohibited in BC
nodes.definition: Sale or planting prohibited in BC.

nodes.label: drought
nodes.definition: Dry spells without irrigation once established.

nodes.label: salt
nodes.definition: Road salt spray or saline soil.

nodes.label: wind
nodes.definition: Strong or persistent wind.

nodes.label: winter wet
nodes.definition: Saturated soil through the wet season.

nodes.label: urban pollution
nodes.definition: Exhaust, dust and compacted soil of streets.

nodes.label: leaf scorch
nodes.definition: Browning of leaf edges from sun, wind or drought.

nodes.label: black walnut
nodes.definition: Juglone, the chemical black walnut roots release, which kills many plants nearby.

nodes.label: deer
nodes.definition: Browsing by deer, a common cause of damage in the North Shore and suburbs.

nodes.label: rabbit
nodes.definition: Browsing by rabbits, mainly on young growth.

nodes.label: pest
nodes.definition: Insect and mite pests in general.

nodes.label: disease
nodes.definition: Fungal, bacterial and viral diseases in general.

nodes.label: Abiotic disorder
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Abiotic disorder': Damage from non-living causes: weather, soil, chemicals.

nodes.label: Adelgids
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Adelgids': Small sap-sucking insects on conifers.

nodes.label: Anthracnose
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Anthracnose': A fungal disease causing leaf and shoot blight, worse in wet springs.

nodes.label: Aphids
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Aphids': Small sap-sucking insects that cluster on new growth.

nodes.label: Bacterial leaf spot
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Bacterial leaf spot': Water-soaked spots on leaves from bacteria.

nodes.label: Beetles or weevils
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Beetles or weevils': Chewing beetles; root weevils notch leaves and eat roots.

nodes.label: Blight or needle cast
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Blight or needle cast': Fungal dieback of shoots or shedding of needles.

nodes.label: Canker or sap rot
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Canker or sap rot': Dead sunken bark patches, often oozing.

nodes.label: Caterpillar or cutworm
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Caterpillar or cutworm': Larvae that chew leaves or cut stems.

nodes.label: Crown rot
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Crown rot': Rot at the base of the plant, usually from wet soil.

nodes.label: Dieback
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Dieback': Progressive death of shoots from the tips.

nodes.label: Fungal leaf spot
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Fungal leaf spot': Spots on leaves caused by fungi.

nodes.label: Galls
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Galls': Abnormal swellings caused by insects or mites.

nodes.label: Leaf miner insect
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Leaf miner insect': Larvae that tunnel inside leaves.

nodes.label: Leaf scorch
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Leaf scorch': Browning of leaf edges from sun, wind or drought.

nodes.label: Mealybugs
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Mealybugs': Woolly white sap-sucking insects.

nodes.label: Mildew
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Mildew': Powdery or downy fungal coating on leaves.

nodes.label: Mites
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Mites': Tiny sap-sucking arachnids causing stippled leaves.

nodes.label: Mold
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Mold': Grey or sooty fungal growth on leaves or flowers.

nodes.label: Nematodes
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Nematodes': Microscopic worms attacking roots.

nodes.label: Root rot
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Root rot': Root decay from fungi in wet soil.

nodes.label: Rust
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Rust': Orange fungal pustules on leaves.

nodes.label: Scale insects
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Scale insects': Immobile sap-sucking insects under a waxy shell.

nodes.label: Slugs or snails
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Slugs or snails': Molluscs that chew holes in leaves.

nodes.label: Thrips
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Thrips': Tiny insects that rasp leaves and flowers.

nodes.label: Virus
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Virus': Viral infection causing mottling or distortion.

nodes.label: Whitefly
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Whitefly': Small white sap-sucking flies.

nodes.label: Wilt
nodes.definition: Pest or disease 'Wilt': Vascular disease causing drooping and death of branches.
